blocks.text: Let's look at this one. Match each inequality with the word that joins its two conditions: and, or or.
blocks.display: Match each inequality with the word that joins its two conditions.

blocks.text: X greater than two and x less than six. And means both at once, so the graph is the overlap.
blocks.display: x > 2 and x < 6 → and: the overlap

blocks.text: Two is less than x, which is less than six. The three-part form is an and in disguise.
X less than two or x greater than six. Or means either one is enough, so the graph is both pieces together.
blocks.display: x < 2 or x > 6 → or: both pieces together

blocks.text: X less than or equal to negative one, or x greater than or equal to four. Or means either one is enough.
blocks.display: x ≤ −1 or x ≥ 4 → or: both pieces together

blocks.text: And means both at once, so the graph is the overlap. Or means either one, so the graph is both pieces together. The three-part form is an and in disguise.
